x: In the handicap our newcomer from Australia walked his best race yet to hold Coates to 1 second and win comfortably, the time 2.26.26- Dave DeBondi.
Dave King showed a powerful return to form on this tough course and both Bob Coates and Dave Debondi walked stormers at their first attempt at 50 Kilos.

It is a tribute to Belgrave that under such conditions we not only finished 25 points clear to win the team title - our first win since 1960 - but also retained the Nijmegan Shield for the first full team of eight to finish. 8th man Dave DeBondi closing the team in 31st position.

Dave DeBondi from Australia has been another credit to our trade account and adding to our reputation as "The International All Stars". On the home front Paul Duckett and Andy Hinchcliff have both produced some good races in preperation for the winter with Paul's 24.50 for fourth place in the Englis…

The forward walking of the other four members of the eight man team; Bob Coates, Pat Duncan, Bob Farley and Dave DeBondi enabled Belgrave to win the Nijmegen Shield awarded to the first team to finish its declared eight.
Pat Duncan is at last coming through a bit although both Brian Ward and Dave King look like catching him ( some hope !) and its good to see Dave Debondi back in the thick of it once more.

Dave Debondi had a disappointing race, mainly due to an unfortunate fall in training, ( Lawton still denies tripping him!) but George Beecham's defeat of John Keown should certainly strengthen our chances in the Brighton where both will be fighting for a team place.

Ray Middleton and Wolly Wortley were our sole representatives on the grid at one minute to go when to their relief John Moullin, Dave DeBondi, Dave King and Pat Duncan all sped into view and after frantic scenes of nudity in the middle of the road the Belgrave team were on their way.
Bob Coates showed good form after a spell away from competition to take third place, and with Carl Lawton fourth and Dave DeBondi sixth, it was a pity there was no team race.
…od preparation for 20-miles. Bob Coates, in a welcome return to the championship team, was only just behind Carl, while Dave DeBondi took another step forward.…
Barry Ingarfield started fast but faded over the second half while Dave DeBondi celebrated his return to fitness by walking the last 10 miles nearly five minutes faster than his first 10.
John Moullin made up our scoring four, while Dave DeBondi looked like a man who'd been doing a bit of training, and long-distance specialist Dave King was only just outside three hours.

This year, we got third place, behind Sheffield and Royal Sutton Coldfield, who seem to be making quite a habit of getting home a place ahead of us these days. John Moullin led our men home, but was only just in front of Bob Coates, while Dave DeBondi was just a fraction outside 5hrs.

Dave DeBondi and Pat Duncan are both training hard - so is Dave King. Nonetheless although we have the greatest depth and strength of any club in the world - witness those packs at Wimbledon-in the present competitive climate it is impossible to relax.

A fine walk by Ray Middleton who finished second to the Israeli Ladany and also a sub 6 Hour clocking from Dave DeBondi, certainly his finest race in this country, gave Belgrave an easy team victory over Surrey Walking Club.
